title: Hand on Heart (Heart Health Weeks) - A prevention project of the Department of Pediatric Cardiology at LMU with the support of the Nicolas May Foundation
summary:
Cardiovascular diseases have been the most common cause of death in Germany for several years and cause high costs for the healthcare system. It is not only older people who are affected: Around 2-4 young people or 1-2 adolescents under the age of 18 die of sudden cardiac death every day in Germany. In addition, disease-causing changes in the heart and blood vessels are sometimes already apparent at a young age.

Despite these facts, a detailed check-up of the cardiovascular system is still missing as part of preventive health examinations in order to detect possible risks at an early stage. Our project enables schoolchildren in the greater Munich area to have a free and detailed examination of their cardiovascular system in order to detect diseases at an early stage and identify individual risk factors. Targeted prevention strategies aim to improve the cardiovascular health of children and young people and prevent the occurrence of diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All pupils in year 5 and above at the participating schools may take part with the written consent of their parents.
Siblings may also take part in the examinations.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent of the study participants or lack of consent of the parents.
If a physical or mental disability does not permit participation in individual examinations, the children and adolescents are excluded from the corresponding examinations.
